title: Robotics & Embodied AI
tagline: Teach robots with data: robot learning basics, imitation learning, ACT, diffusion policies, vision-language-action models, and sim-to-real.
prereqs: Reinforcement Learning. Deep Learning. Hardware: step 9 wants a recent NVIDIA GPU or a cloud GPU; step 10 needs a physical SO-101 arm, so treat it as optional and use the ACT and Diffusion Policy steps with LeRobot simulation datasets instead.

steps.title: Introduction to robot learning
steps.why: What makes learning for robots different from other ML.

steps.title: Imitation learning
steps.why: Behavior cloning, its failure modes, and common fixes.

steps.title: ALOHA and Action Chunking Transformers
steps.why: Predict chunks of actions for smooth, precise manipulation.

steps.title: Diffusion policy
steps.why: Generate robot actions with diffusion models.

steps.title: Vision-language-action models
steps.why: How LLM-style models become robot controllers.

steps.title: VLA models compared
steps.why: OpenVLA, pi0, and RT-2 side by side.

steps.title: Pi0: a generalist robot policy
steps.why: A flow-matching VLA trained across many robots.

steps.title: Robot foundation models
steps.why: Sergey Levine on where generalist robot models are headed.

steps.title: Reinforcement learning for robots in simulation
steps.why: Train locomotion policies in Isaac Lab.

steps.title: Optional: train a real robot arm with LeRobot
steps.why: Hardware-dependent: collect demos and train a policy on a low-cost arm.

projects: Train an ACT or diffusion policy in LeRobot on a public dataset and report success rate in simulation.
Write behavior cloning for a simulated task and show where it drifts, then add DAgger-style corrections.
Train a quadruped to walk in Isaac Lab and compare two reward designs.
